annotations.description: Mulliganed a 7-card hand that had 4 lands, a 4-drop creature (Inspiring Unicorn), a cantrip (Acrobatic Maneuver), and Flicker of Fate. While the hand is slow with no early plays and the flicker effects lack strong ETB targets, it's functional with guaranteed mana and a card-draw spell to find more action.
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. It has sufficient lands, a turn-4 play, and Acrobatic Maneuver to cycle into more threats. Going to 6 risks a worse hand for marginal improvement.

annotations.description: Used Diabolic Edict to remove a 2/2 Ronom Unicorn when Takenuma Bleeder (3/3) could have been deployed instead, which would outclass it in combat. The Edict is better saved for higher-value targets. Alternatively, Spawning Pit would enable morbid synergies for the powerful Morkrut Banshee and Reaper from the Abyss in hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Diabolic Edict to sacrifice opponent's Ronom Unicorn 2/2
annotations.betterLine: Cast Takenuma Bleeder (3/3 that outclasses the 2/2) to develop the board and save Diabolic Edict for a larger threat, or cast Spawning Pit to set up morbid synergies for Morkrut Banshee and Reaper from the Abyss.

annotations.description: Cast Flicker of Fate with no meaningful target - GPT54 Sport controls no creatures or enchantments to blink for value. Flickering the opponent's Takenuma Bleeder accomplishes nothing. This wastes a card and 2 mana that could have been used productively. With a land drop remaining, they could play a land and cast Inspiring Unicorn (4 mana) to start building a board presence against the opponent's 3/3.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Flicker of Fate targeting presumably the opponent's Takenuma Bleeder, wasting a card for no effect.
annotations.betterLine: Play a land first, then cast Inspiring Unicorn for {2}{W}{W} to establish board presence. Alternatively, pass and hold up Flicker of Fate for a future turn when you have your own creatures to blink for value.

annotations.description: Flicker of Fate was cast on the opponent's Takenuma Bleeder, which already had summoning sickness. Flickering it just returns it to the battlefield still with summoning sickness - accomplishing nothing while wasting a card and 2 mana. Flicker of Fate is extremely valuable in this hand for blinking own ETB creatures like Wispweaver Angel later.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Flicker of Fate targeting opponent's Takenuma Bleeder (which already had summoning sickness)
annotations.betterLine: Play a land and pass, saving Flicker of Fate for blinking own ETB creatures (Wispweaver Angel, or creatures buffed by Emiel the Blessed) later in the game for actual card advantage.

annotations.description: Blocking Takenuma Bleeder with Mesa Unicorn trades away a key unicorn synergy piece (for Emiel the Blessed and Inspiring Unicorn in hand) without even killing the Bleeder (3/3 survives 2 damage). Mesa Unicorn's lifelink is especially valuable with the upcoming Inspiring Unicorn pump effects and Emiel's +1/+1 counters.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Takenuma Bleeder with Mesa Unicorn, losing the unicorn and only saving ~5 life (going to 15 instead of 10)
annotations.betterLine: Take the 7 damage (going to 10), preserve Mesa Unicorn for the powerful unicorn engine with Emiel the Blessed and Inspiring Unicorn. The lifelink on Mesa Unicorn would recoup life over subsequent turns, especially when buffed.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 9 life with no untapped creatures or lands to interact. Attacking with all four available creatures (Reaper 6 + Banshee 4 + Shambler 4 + Bleeder 3 = 17) is lethal. The player only sent Takenuma Bleeder and Suspicious Shambler for 7 damage, leaving the opponent alive at 2 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Takenuma Bleeder (3) and Suspicious Shambler (4) for 7 total damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all four creatures (Reaper from the Abyss, Morkrut Banshee, Suspicious Shambler, Takenuma Bleeder) for 17 damage, which is lethal against the opponent's 9 life with no blockers available.

annotations.description: Failed to cast Spawning Pit with 4 untapped Swamps available. Spawning Pit costs only {2} and provides a sacrifice outlet that could trigger Reaper from the Abyss's morbid ability (destroy target non-Demon creature at end step). While the board is already dominant with opponent at 2 life, casting it is free value with no downside.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Spawning Pit
annotations.betterLine: Cast Spawning Pit for {2} using two untapped Swamps. This provides a sacrifice outlet that synergizes with Reaper from the Abyss's morbid trigger and adds insurance against the opponent's 5-card hand potentially finding answers.

annotations.description: At 2 life facing lethal on board (Reaper from the Abyss 6/6 flying, Fetid Imp 1/2 flying, Morkrut Banshee 4/4 untapped), the player passed their main phase without casting anything. They had Valorous Stance to destroy Reaper from the Abyss and enough mana for a 4-drop creature as a blocker. Passing guarantees death next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in precombat main phase, casting nothing despite having 4 mana and multiple playable spells.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Valorous Stance targeting Reaper from the Abyss to remove the 6/6 flyer, then cast a creature (Emiel the Blessed or Inspiring Unicorn for {2}{W}{W}) as a blocker. This at least removes the biggest threat and provides a body to block Morkrut Banshee, giving a slim chance of survival.

annotations.description: Declined to activate Fetid Imp's deathtouch ability during combat when 3 untapped Swamps were available. With the opponent at 2 life facing 4 attackers, giving the Imp deathtouch is pure upside - it forces any potential blocker to trade with it, making the opponent's blocking decisions worse.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Fetid Imp's deathtouch ability
annotations.betterLine: Activate Fetid Imp's {B} deathtouch ability to make it trade with any blocker, using one of the three available untapped Swamps
